points.text: Theoretical analysis forced, restates setup, vague claims, unclear link to empirical results
Pretraining baselines on same small dataset undercuts baselines designed for large unlabeled data
Unseen sensor placement experiments need more detailed study
Purpose of Figure 3 qualitative visualizations unclear
Redundant wording at line 348
Unclear what the 'structural' factors actually are
Paper opaque to readers outside the field
Unclear why contrastive positive pairs share identical S and R elements
Unclear if SPAR uses spatial info at evaluation while baselines don't; gain source confounded
Generalization and ablation evidence for key claims relegated to appendix; task generalization not shown
Experimental validation listed as separate contribution
Term 'duality' between positions and signals misused
Equation 6 bound lacks citation or novelty claim
Unclear whether embeddings are summed or concatenated
Figures 4 and 5 referenced out of order
Limited novelty: standard embeddings, LLM as preprocessing, known dual reconstruction
Manual normalization of spatial inputs unjustified given learned embedding
Structural position concept ill-defined; unclear embedding captures semantic placement
Datasets with meaningful structural attributes unspecified; no analysis of structural effect
Proposition 3.1 hard to follow and does not support stated claims; weak theory-method link
Baseline result provenance unclear; some baselines extremely poor without explanation
LLM component evaluated only on HAR with minimal improvement
No runtime or computational complexity reported
Comparisons unfair since baselines do not use spatial information
Model size/complexity not reported, so gains may come from capacity
Ablation should report complexity impact of dropped components
Proposition 3.1 relies on strong assumptions; bound does not show better representations
Claim of avoiding redundant memorization not shown
Proposition 3.2 is analogy, not theorem; image-patch argument may not transfer
'Solid theoretical foundations' overstated; theory unlinked to measurable properties
Limited novelty relative to existing position-aware MAE variants
Placement-aware MAE baselines and same-embedding controls missing
Unclear whether baselines receive position/node info; comparison conflates access with objective
Spatial-reconstruction objective may reduce to trivial scene/node identification
Unclear whether structural embeddings are shared across scenes or tied to nodes
Localization coordinate frame normalization and de-normalization unclear
Unseen-placement test uses single similar held-out scene; no truly new layout
No test of transfer to new body placements or subjects on HAR
Per-node learned embeddings cannot handle new nodes, contradicting arbitrary-placement claim
Gains on Ridgecrest and HAR small and within noise; 'superior' unwarranted
Clear gain only on authors' own M3N-VC dataset
Ablations only on M3N-VC, missing for Ridgecrest and HAR
Pretraining includes downstream scene, making unseen comparisons split-dependent
Only frozen-encoder evaluation; full fine-tuning not tested
Contrastive baselines extremely poor, suggesting poor tuning or fit
Same epochs for all methods; no baseline hyperparameter search
Noisy GPS labels may dominate localization error and compress differences
No supervised, non-pretrained or classical localization comparison
No cost analysis: parameter count, pretraining time
No scaling or transfer experiments despite foundation-model framing
Structural-position interpretation heuristic; no probing of learned structural vectors
